title: The Work of Raising the Next Generation of Men Why manners, character, and example still matter
author: Chris Martin
source: The Ways of a Gentleman (Martin Substack), January 29, 2026
summary: Martin argues that raising boys to become men of character is serious, intentional work that requires fathers and mentors to model what they wish to see rather than simply telling boys what to do. He contends that boys learn masculinity not through ideology or lecture but through observation and imitation of the men around them. Martin emphasizes that example is the most powerful teacher—boys notice how their fathers handle stress, treat their wives, keep their word, manage money, and carry themselves in public. The work is not glamorous or quick but requires years of consistent modeling, correction, and reinforcement. Martin calls for a return to intentional male mentorship and formation, arguing that the stakes are high because these young men will become the leaders and fathers of the next generation.
points: Boys learn masculinity through observation and imitation of the men around them, not through ideology or lecture—example is the most powerful teacher.
Fathers and mentors must model what they wish to see: how to handle stress, how to treat women, how to keep commitments, how to manage resources, how to carry oneself with dignity.
The work of raising the next generation of men is not glamorous or quick but requires years of consistent modeling, correction, and reinforcement.
Character is caught, not taught—boys absorb far more from what they observe in their father's daily life than from any explicit instruction.
The stakes are high because these young men will become the leaders, fathers, and builders of the next generation—their formation shapes not just families but institutions and culture.
